source.text: וַיְהִ֧י אֲרוֹן־יְהוָ֛ה בִּשְׂדֵ֥ה פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים שִׁבְעָ֥ה חֳדָשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: And was [the] ark of Yahweh in [the] territory of [the] Philistines seven months.

en.L: And the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was in the territory of [the] Philistines seven months.
en.B: The ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was in the land of the Philistines for seven months.
en.R: The ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stayed in Philistine territory for seven months.

decisions.choice: the ark of Yahweh: the chest that stood for Yahweh's presence, captured by the Philistines
decisions.reason: The Philistines had taken the ark in battle (4:11) and moved it from Ashdod to Gath to Ekron, and each city was struck with a plague (5:1-12). This chapter tells how they sent it back.

decisions.choice: territory of the Philistines: the whole Philistine country, not only open fields
decisions.reason: The word usually means "field", but it can name the open country or region belonging to a people (Genesis 32:4; Ruth 1:1). The ark had been in several Philistine cities, so the region as a whole is meant.

decisions.choice: the land of the Philistines (Balanced); Philistine territory (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both say plainly that the region is meant, not farmland.

source.text: וַיִּקְרְא֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים לַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים וְלַקֹּֽסְמִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַֽה־נַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה לַאֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה הוֹדִעֻ֕נוּ בַּמֶּ֖ה נְשַׁלְּחֶ֥נּוּ לִמְקוֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And called [the] Philistines for the priests and for the diviners, saying, What shall we do with [the] ark of Yahweh? Make known to us with what we shall send it to its place.

en.L: And [the] Philistines called for the priests and for the diviners, saying, "What shall we do with the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? Make known to us with what we shall send it to its place."
en.B: Then the Philistines summoned the priests and the diviners and said, "What should we do with the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? Tell us what we should send with it when we send it back to its place."
en.R: Then the Philistines called for their priests and for the men who claimed to learn hidden things from signs. They asked, "What should we do with the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}? Tell us what we should send along with it when we send it back to where it belongs."

decisions.choice: diviners: people who claimed to learn hidden things or the future from signs and omens
decisions.reason: Divination was common among Israel's neighbors and forbidden in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10, 14). The Philistines call on their own religious experts to explain what has happened and what to do.

decisions.choice: with what: with what gift the ark should go back
alternatives: how shall we send it to its place?
decisions.reason: The question can mean "how" or "with what". The answer in verses 3-5, a guilt offering of gold sent along with the ark, shows that they are asking what should go with it.

decisions.choice: its place: the ark's own home among the Israelites
decisions.reason: The ark belonged with the people of the God of Israel, not in a Philistine temple (5:2-4, 11).

decisions.choice: the men who claimed to learn hidden things from signs
decisions.reason: Readable explains "diviners", a word many readers do not know, and says "their priests" because these are the Philistines' own priests.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אִֽם־מְשַׁלְּחִ֞ים אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אַל־תְּשַׁלְּח֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ רֵיקָ֔ם כִּֽי־הָשֵׁ֥ב תָּשִׁ֛יבוּ ל֖וֹ אָשָׁ֑ם אָ֤ז תֵּרָֽפְאוּ֙ וְנוֹדַ֣ע לָכֶ֔ם לָ֛מָּה לֹא־תָס֥וּר יָד֖וֹ מִכֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, If [you are] sending [the] ark of [the] God of Israel, do not send it empty, but surely return to him a guilt offering; then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why not turns aside his hand from you.

en.L: And they said, "If you [are] sending away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it away empty, but you must surely return to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand does not turn aside from you."
en.B: They answered, "If you are sending the ark of the God of Israel away, you must not send it empty. Be sure to return a guilt offering to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then you will be healed, and you will know why {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand has not been taken away from you."
en.R: They answered, "If you send away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it back with nothing. You must send {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a guilt offering to make up for the wrong you have done. Then you will be healed, and you will know why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has kept on punishing you."

decisions.choice: guilt offering: a payment that makes up for a wrong done
decisions.reason: The word is the name of the guilt offering in Leviticus 5:14-26, where someone who has wronged what is holy pays it back and adds more. The Philistines had taken what belonged to Israel's God, so they return the ark with a payment of gold (verses 4-5, 8).

decisions.choice: his hand does not turn aside: he keeps on striking you
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for God's power in action. In chapter 5 his hand was heavy on each city that held the ark (5:6, 7, 9, 11).

decisions.choice: you will know why his hand has not left you: once you are healed, it will be clear that his hand was the cause
alternatives: then you will be healed, and it will become known to you why his hand did not turn from you
and atonement will be made for you; will his hand not then turn from you?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short and can be read in more than one way. Read as it stands, healing after the offering will show that it was the God of Israel who had been striking them. The ancient Greek translation has "and atonement will be made for you; should not his hand then leave you?", which may reflect a different Hebrew text. The test in verse 9 takes up the same question of whether his hand was really the cause.

decisions.choice: a guilt offering to make up for the wrong you have done; he has kept on punishing you
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a guilt offering is for and says plainly what "his hand has not turned aside" means.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ מָ֣ה הָאָשָׁם֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נָשִׁ֣יב לוֹ֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ מִסְפַּר֙ סַרְנֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים חֲמִשָּׁה֙ טְחֹרֵ֣י זָהָ֔ב וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה עַכְבְּרֵ֣י זָהָ֑ב כִּֽי־מַגֵּפָ֥ה אַחַ֛ת לְכֻלָּ֖ם וּלְסַרְנֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said, What [is] the guilt offering which we shall return to him? And they said, [The] number of [the] rulers of [the] Philistines: five tumors of gold and five mice of gold, for one plague [is] to all of them and to your rulers.

en.L: And they said, "What [is] the guilt offering that we shall return to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?" And they said, "[By the] number of the rulers of [the] Philistines, five tumors of gold and five rats of gold, for one plague [was] on all of them and on your rulers.
en.B: They asked, "What guilt offering should we return to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?" They answered, "Five gold tumors and five gold rats, one for each of the rulers of the Philistines, because the same plague struck all the people and your rulers.
en.R: The Philistines asked, "What guilt offering should we send back to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?" The priests and diviners answered, "Send five gold tumors and five gold rats, one for each of the five Philistine rulers. The same plague has struck all your people and your rulers.

decisions.choice: rulers of the Philistines: the lords of the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: This title is used only for the Philistine rulers. There were five of them, one each for Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron (verse 17; Joshua 13:3; Judges 3:3).

decisions.choice: tumors: swellings on the body
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text here, as in 5:6-12 and 6:5, has a word that means "mounds" or "swellings". The scribes' tradition for reading aloud replaces it with another word for tumors or swellings, perhaps a more polite one. Either way the plague caused painful swellings. What disease it was is not certain; some think of the swellings of bubonic plague, which rats spread, and the older word "emerods" (hemorrhoids) reflects another guess.

decisions.choice: rats: rodents that were ruining the land (verse 5)
decisions.reason: The word names a small rodent, a mouse or a rat; the language does not separate the two. Since these creatures were destroying the land (verse 5) and the plague brought swellings, a rat plague is likely, but the word itself does not settle which animal is meant.

decisions.choice: all of them and your rulers: the whole people and their rulers alike
decisions.reason: The speakers shift from "them" to "your". "All of them" is the Philistine people, and the same plague struck the rulers too, so each ruler sends an offering for his city.

decisions.choice: one for each of the rulers; all the people
decisions.reason: "The number of the rulers" means one gold image for each ruler, which Balanced and Readable say plainly. Both say "the people" for "all of them", and Readable names who is speaking in each half of the verse.

source.text: וַעֲשִׂיתֶם֩ צַלְמֵ֨י טְחֹרֵיכֶ֜ם וְצַלְמֵ֣י עַכְבְּרֵיכֶ֗ם הַמַּשְׁחִיתִם֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וּנְתַתֶּ֛ם לֵאלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כָּב֑וֹד אוּלַ֗י יָקֵ֤ל אֶת־יָדוֹ֙ מֵֽעֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וּמֵעַ֥ל אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם וּמֵעַ֥ל אַרְצְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make images of your tumors and images of your mice that are ruining the land, and you will give to [the] God of Israel glory; perhaps he will lighten his hand from on you and from on your gods and from on your land.

en.L: And you will make images of your tumors and images of your rats that are ruining the land, and you will give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lighten {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand from on you and from on your gods and from on your land.
en.B: So make images of your tumors and images of your rats that are destroying the land, and give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will lighten {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand on you, on your gods and on your land.
en.R: Make gold models of your tumors and of the rats that are ruining your land. In this way, give honor to the God of Israel. Then perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will stop punishing you and your gods and your land so heavily.

decisions.choice: the rats that are ruining the land: rodents swarming over Philistine country
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text of chapter 5 speaks only of tumors; the rats appear for the first time here, as if the reader already knows of them. The ancient Greek translation mentions mice spreading through the land already in 5:6 and 6:1.

decisions.choice: give glory to the God of Israel: openly admit his power and that he has been wronged
decisions.reason: To give glory to God can mean to confess the truth before him (Joshua 7:19). The gold images admit that the plague came from him. The word "glory" is related to "heavy": his hand was heavy on them (5:6, 11), and now they honor him so that he will make it light.

decisions.choice: lighten his hand: ease the punishment
decisions.reason: The picture of a heavy hand pressing down on someone (5:6, 11) is turned around: they hope he will lift its weight.

decisions.choice: your gods: the Philistine gods, Dagon among them
decisions.reason: Dagon's image had fallen and broken before the ark (5:2-5), so the speakers count their own gods among those struck.

decisions.choice: gold models; honor
decisions.reason: Readable says "models" for "images" and adds that they are gold, as verse 4 says. It uses "honor" for "glory", which here means showing respect.

source.text: וְלָ֤מָּה תְכַבְּדוּ֙ אֶת־לְבַבְכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר כִּבְּד֛וּ מִצְרַ֥יִם וּפַרְעֹ֖ה אֶת־לִבָּ֑ם הֲלוֹא֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר הִתְעַלֵּ֣ל בָּהֶ֔ם וַֽיְשַׁלְּח֖וּם וַיֵּלֵֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And why will you make heavy your heart as made heavy Egypt and Pharaoh their heart? Was it not when he dealt harshly with them, and they sent them away, and they went?

en.L: And why will you make your heart heavy, just as Egypt and Pharaoh made their heart heavy? Was it not when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had dealt harshly with them that they sent them away, and they went?
en.B: Why harden your hearts the way the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened theirs? Once {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had dealt harshly with them, did they not let the Israelites go, and they left?
en.R: Do not be stubborn the way the Egyptians and Pharaoh were. After God had punished them severely, they let the Israelites go, and the Israelites left Egypt.

decisions.choice: make your heart heavy: refuse to give in, as Pharaoh did
decisions.reason: The words recall the plagues in Egypt, where Pharaoh made his heart heavy and would not let Israel go (Exodus 8:11, 28; 9:34). The Philistines already knew that this God had struck Egypt (4:8). "Heavy" also ties in with the heavy hand of God (5:6, 11) and the glory of verse 5.

decisions.choice: dealt harshly: made sport of them, made them look foolish by his power
decisions.reason: The same verb is used when Yahweh tells how he dealt with Egypt (Exodus 10:2). It means to act against someone at will, showing them up as powerless.

decisions.choice: they sent them away, and they went: the Egyptians let the Israelites go
decisions.reason: The first "they" is the Egyptians and the second "them" is Israel, as in the Exodus story (Exodus 12:31-33).

decisions.choice: the Israelites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the Israelites so that the pronouns are clear. Readable also gives "God" for "he" and turns the speaker's questions into plain statements, which say the same thing.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה קְח֨וּ וַעֲשׂ֜וּ עֲגָלָ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ אֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּ֤י פָרוֹת֙ עָל֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹא־עָלָ֥ה עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עֹ֑ל וַאֲסַרְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־הַפָּרוֹת֙ בָּעֲגָלָ֔ה וַהֲשֵׁיבֹתֶ֧ם בְּנֵיהֶ֛ם מֵאַחֲרֵיהֶ֖ם הַבָּֽיְתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And now take and make one new cart and two nursing cows on which not has come up a yoke, and harness the cows to the cart, and take back their young from after them home.

en.L: And now take and prepare one new cart and two nursing cows on which no yoke has come, and harness the cows to the cart, and take their calves back home from behind them.
en.B: Now then, get a new cart ready, and two cows that are nursing calves and have never been yoked. Harness the cows to the cart, but take their calves away from them and back home.
en.R: So get a new cart ready. Find two cows that are nursing calves and have never pulled a load. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take their calves home, away from their mothers.

decisions.choice: a new cart and cows never yoked: things not used before, fit for a holy purpose
decisions.reason: Animals that had never borne a yoke were set apart for special rites in Israel (Numbers 19:2; Deuteronomy 21:3). Unused things were fitting for carrying the ark.

decisions.choice: nursing cows whose calves are taken away: cows that will naturally want to go back to their calves
decisions.reason: Cows that had never been yoked would not pull together well, and cows separated from their calves would turn back toward them. If they went straight away from home instead, it would be a sign (verse 9).

decisions.choice: never pulled a load
decisions.reason: Readable explains being yoked by what it means for the cows.

source.text: וּלְקַחְתֶּ֞ם אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֗ה וּנְתַתֶּ֤ם אֹתוֹ֙ אֶל־הָ֣עֲגָלָ֔ה וְאֵ֣ת׀כְּלֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֗ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֲשֵׁבֹתֶ֥ם לוֹ֙ אָשָׁ֔ם תָּשִׂ֥ימוּ בָאַרְגַּ֖ז מִצִּדּ֑וֹ וְשִׁלַּחְתֶּ֥ם אֹת֖וֹ וְהָלָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And take [the] ark of Yahweh and put it on the cart, and the articles of gold which you are returning to him [as] a guilt offering put in a box at its side; and send it away, and it will go.

en.L: And take the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and put it on the cart, and the articles of gold that you are returning to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [as] a guilt offering, put [them] in a box at its side. And send it away, and it will go.
en.B: Take the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and set it on the cart, and put the gold objects that you are returning to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as a guilt offering in a box beside it. Then send it off and let it go its way.
en.R: Put the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the cart. Put the gold objects in a box beside it. They are your guilt offering to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then send the cart off and let it go on its own.

decisions.choice: box: a chest or case for carrying valuables
decisions.reason: The word is found only in this chapter (verses 8, 11, 15). It names a container set beside the ark, not inside it.

decisions.choice: send it away, and it will go: let it go with no one driving it
decisions.reason: No driver goes with the cart. Where it goes is left to the cows, which is the point of the test in verse 9.

decisions.choice: three short sentences
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long instruction into steps and says "the cart" so it is clear what is sent off.

source.text: וּרְאִיתֶ֗ם אִם־דֶּ֨רֶךְ גְּבוּל֤וֹ יַֽעֲלֶה֙ בֵּ֣ית שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ ה֚וּא עָ֣שָׂה לָ֔נוּ אֶת־הָרָעָ֥ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את וְאִם־לֹ֗א וְיָדַ֨עְנוּ֙ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָדוֹ֙ נָ֣גְעָה בָּ֔נוּ מִקְרֶ֥ה ה֖וּא הָ֥יָה לָֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And see: if [the] way of its territory it goes up, Beth-shemesh, he has done to us this great evil; and if not, then we will know that not his hand touched us; chance it [was that] happened to us.

en.L: And watch: if it goes up by the way of its own territory, [to] Beth-shemesh, [then] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done to us this great evil. But if not, then we will know that [it was] not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand [that] struck us; it [was] chance [that] happened to us."
en.B: Then watch. If it goes up the road to its own territory, toward Beth-shemesh, then it is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} who has brought this great disaster on us. But if not, we will know that it was not {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand that struck us. It just happened to us by chance."
en.R: Then watch it. If it goes up the road toward Beth-shemesh, back to the ark's own land, then the God of Israel is the one who brought this terrible trouble on us. But if it goes some other way, then we will know that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not the one who struck us. It was only something that happened by chance."

decisions.choice: Beth-shemesh: an Israelite town on the border nearest Philistine land
decisions.reason: Beth-shemesh lay in the valley of Sorek, the first Israelite town on the road from Ekron, and it was one of the towns given to the priests (Joshua 15:10; 21:16).

decisions.choice: he has done: he himself, the God of Israel, is the one who did it
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds the pronoun for emphasis. The test is meant to show whether this God, and no other cause, brought the plague.

decisions.choice: evil: disaster, harm
decisions.reason: The word here means harm suffered, not wrongdoing.

decisions.choice: chance: something that simply happens, with no one causing it
decisions.reason: The same word is used of Ruth "happening" to come to Boaz's field (Ruth 2:3). The diviners leave room for the plague to have been bad luck.

decisions.choice: back to the ark's own land; the God of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says whose territory is meant and names the God of Israel for the emphatic "he".

source.text: וַיַּעֲשׂ֤וּ הָאֲנָשִׁים֙ כֵּ֔ן וַיִּקְח֗וּ שְׁתֵּ֤י פָרוֹת֙ עָל֔וֹת וַיַּאַסְר֖וּם בָּעֲגָלָ֑ה וְאֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם כָּל֥וּ בַבָּֽיִת׃

records.literal_gloss: And did the men so, and they took two nursing cows and harnessed them to the cart, and their young they shut up at home.

en.L: And the men did so, and they took two nursing cows and harnessed them to the cart, and their calves they shut up at home.
en.B: The men did this. They took two cows that were nursing calves and harnessed them to the cart, and they penned up their calves at home.
en.R: The men did what they were told. They took two mother cows and hitched them to the cart. They kept the calves shut up at home.

decisions.choice: the men did so: the Philistines followed the advice exactly
decisions.reason: Each step of verses 7-8 is carried out in verses 10-11.

decisions.choice: mother cows
decisions.reason: Readable says "mother cows" for cows nursing calves, as in verse 7.

source.text: וַיָּשִׂ֛מוּ אֶת־אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־הָעֲגָלָ֑ה וְאֵ֣ת הָאַרְגַּ֗ז וְאֵת֙ עַכְבְּרֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב וְאֵ֖ת צַלְמֵ֥י טְחֹרֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they put [the] ark of Yahweh on the cart, and the box, and the mice of gold, and the images of their tumors.

en.L: And they put the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the cart, and the box, and the rats of gold, and the images of their tumors.
en.B: They set the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the cart, along with the box, the gold rats and the images of their tumors.
en.R: They put the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the cart. They also put the box on it with the gold rats and the gold models of their tumors.

decisions.choice: the box and the gold rats and images: the box holding the gold offering
decisions.reason: Verse 8 told them to put the gold objects in the box, so the list names the box together with what was in it.

decisions.choice: the box ... with; gold models
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the gold objects were in the box, and says they were gold as verse 4 does.

source.text: וַיִשַּׁ֨רְנָההַפָּר֜וֹת בַּדֶּ֗רֶךְ עַל־דֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ בֵּ֣ית שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ בִּמְסִלָּ֣ה אַחַ֗ת הָלְכ֤וּ הָלֹךְ֙ וְגָע֔וֹ וְלֹא־סָ֖רוּ יָמִ֣ין וּשְׂמֹ֑אול וְסַרְנֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ הֹלְכִ֣ים אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם עַד־גְּב֖וּל בֵּ֥ית שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went straight the cows on the way, on [the] way of Beth-shemesh; on one highway they went, going and lowing, and not they turned aside right or left; and [the] rulers of [the] Philistines [were] walking after them as far as [the] border of Beth-shemesh.

en.L: And the cows went straight on the road, on the road to Beth-shemesh. On one highway they went, lowing as they went, and they did not turn aside [to the] right or [to the] left. And the rulers of [the] Philistines [were] walking behind them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.
en.B: The cows went straight along the road toward Beth-shemesh. They kept to the one highway, lowing as they went, and did not turn to the right or the left. The rulers of the Philistines walked behind them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.
en.R: The cows headed straight for Beth-shemesh. They stayed on the main road, mooing all the way, and did not turn off to either side. The Philistine rulers followed them as far as the edge of Beth-shemesh.

decisions.choice: the cows went straight: the sign of verse 9 is given
decisions.reason: Cows that had never been yoked, taken from their calves, would be expected to wander or turn back home. They went straight to Israel's border, showing that the God of Israel had sent the plague and was bringing his ark home.

decisions.choice: lowing as they went: crying out for their calves
decisions.reason: The cows called for their calves the whole way and yet did not turn back to them, which makes the sign stronger.

decisions.choice: the rulers walked behind: they watched the test themselves
decisions.reason: The five rulers followed to see the outcome with their own eyes, and stopped at the border of Israelite land.

decisions.choice: mooing; did not turn off to either side
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for a cow's call and says "to either side" for "right or left".

source.text: וּבֵ֣ית שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ קֹצְרִ֥ים קְצִיר־חִטִּ֖ים בָּעֵ֑מֶק וַיִּשְׂא֣וּ אֶת־עֵינֵיהֶ֗ם וַיִּרְאוּ֙ אֶת־הָ֣אָר֔וֹן וַֽיִּשְׂמְח֖וּ לִרְאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And Beth-shemesh [were] reaping [the] harvest of wheat in the valley, and they lifted their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see [it].

en.L: And [the people of] Beth-shemesh [were] reaping [the] wheat harvest in the valley, and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see [it].
en.B: Now the people of Beth-shemesh were out in the valley reaping the wheat harvest. When they looked up and saw the ark, they were glad at the sight.
en.R: The people of Beth-shemesh were cutting their wheat in the valley. They looked up and saw the ark, and they were full of joy to see it.

decisions.choice: Beth-shemesh: the people of the town
decisions.reason: The town's name stands for the people who lived there, and the verbs that follow are plural.

decisions.choice: the wheat harvest: late spring, around May and June
decisions.reason: Wheat was harvested after barley, in the weeks before the Festival of Weeks (Exodus 34:22). The townspeople were out in the fields of the valley below the town.

decisions.choice: lifted up their eyes: looked up
decisions.reason: The phrase means to look up and notice something, often with surprise (Genesis 22:4).

decisions.choice: the people of Beth-shemesh
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who was reaping.

source.text: וְהָעֲגָלָ֡ה בָּ֠אָה אֶל־שְׂדֵ֨ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ בֵּֽית־הַשִּׁמְשִׁי֙ וַתַּעֲמֹ֣ד שָׁ֔ם וְשָׁ֖ם אֶ֣בֶן גְּדוֹלָ֑ה וַֽיְבַקְּעוּ֙ אֶת־עֲצֵ֣י הָעֲגָלָ֔ה וְאֶת־הַ֨פָּר֔וֹת הֶעֱל֥וּ עֹלָ֖ה לַיהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And the cart came to [the] field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite and stood there, and there [was] a large stone; and they split the wood of the cart, and the cows they offered up [as] a burnt offering to Yahweh.

en.L: And the cart came to the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite and stopped there, and there [was] a large stone there. And they split the wood of the cart, and they offered up the cows [as] a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The cart reached the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh and stopped there, where there was a large stone. The people split up the cart's wood and sacrificed the cows to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a burnt offering.
en.R: The cart came into a field that belonged to a man named Joshua from Beth-shemesh. It stopped there, where there was a large rock. The people broke up the cart for firewood and offered the cows as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Joshua the Beth-shemeshite: a landowner of the town, not Joshua son of Nun
decisions.reason: He is named only here and in verse 18. Naming the owner of the field tells the first readers where the stone could be found.

decisions.choice: the cart and the cows offered: what had carried the ark was not put back to common use
decisions.reason: The cart and cows had served a holy purpose, so the people burned them as an offering to Yahweh. Leviticus 1:3 asks for a male animal for a burnt offering, but the story does not stop to comment on that.

decisions.choice: they split ... they offered: the people of Beth-shemesh
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; the people who had run to see the ark (verse 13) are meant. Verse 15 adds that Levites took the ark down.

decisions.choice: the people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject. Readable says the cart was broken up "for firewood" because that is why its wood was split.

source.text: וְהַלְוִיִּ֞ם הוֹרִ֣ידוּ׀אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֗ה וְאֶת־הָאַרְגַּ֤ז אֲשֶׁר־אִתּוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁר־בּ֣וֹ כְלֵֽי־זָהָ֔ב וַיָּשִׂ֖מוּ אֶל־הָאֶ֣בֶן הַגְּדוֹלָ֑ה וְאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית־שֶׁ֗מֶשׁ הֶעֱל֨וּ עֹל֜וֹת וַֽיִּזְבְּח֧וּ זְבָחִ֛ים בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לַֽיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the Levites brought down [the] ark of Yahweh and the box which [was] with it, which in it [were the] articles of gold, and they put [them] on the large stone; and [the] men of Beth-shemesh offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices on that day to Yahweh.

en.L: And the Levites took down the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the box that [was] with it, in which [were the] articles of gold, and they put [them] on the large stone. And the men of Beth-shemesh offered up burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices on that day to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The Levites had taken down the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the box with it that held the gold objects, and had set them on the large stone. On that day the men of Beth-shemesh brought burnt offerings and other sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The Levites had already lifted down the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the box with the gold objects in it. They had set them on the large rock. That same day the men of Beth-shemesh gave burnt offerings and other sacrifices to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the Levites: the tribe set apart to carry the ark
decisions.reason: Only the Levites were to carry the ark (Numbers 4:15; Deuteronomy 10:8). Beth-shemesh was one of the towns given to the priests of Levi's tribe (Joshua 21:16), so Levites lived there.

decisions.choice: took down: done before the cart was burned
decisions.reason: The verse goes back to say what happened to the ark before the cart was broken up and burned in verse 14. The Levites lifted it off and set it on the stone first.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and sacrifices: offerings wholly burned and offerings shared in a meal
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was burned entirely on the altar. The other sacrifices were partly burned and partly eaten by the worshipers, as a meal of thanks (Leviticus 1; 3).

decisions.choice: had taken down; had set
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "had" to show that this was done before the burning in verse 14.

source.text: וַחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה סַרְנֵֽי־פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים רָא֑וּ וַיָּשֻׁ֥בוּ עֶקְר֖וֹן בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And five rulers of Philistines saw, and they returned [to] Ekron on that day.

en.L: And [the] five rulers of [the] Philistines saw [it], and they returned [to] Ekron on that day.
en.B: When the five rulers of the Philistines had seen this, they went back to Ekron that same day.
en.R: The five Philistine rulers watched all this. Then they went back to Ekron that same day.

decisions.choice: Ekron: the nearest Philistine city, where the ark had last been held
decisions.reason: The ark had been sent from Gath to Ekron, and the people of Ekron demanded that it be sent away (5:10-12). The road from Ekron ran east to Beth-shemesh.

decisions.choice: saw: saw what had happened, the cows' journey and the welcome at Beth-shemesh
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; the whole scene is meant. The rulers saw the sign for themselves.

decisions.choice: this; all this
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "saw".

source.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ טְחֹרֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵשִׁ֧יבוּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֛ים אָשָׁ֖ם לַֽיהוָ֑ה לְאַשְׁדּ֨וֹד אֶחָ֜דלְעַזָּ֤ה אֶחָד֙ לְאַשְׁקְל֣וֹן אֶחָ֔ד לְגַ֥ת אֶחָ֖ד לְעֶקְר֥וֹן אֶחָֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And these [are] the tumors of gold which returned [the] Philistines [as] a guilt offering to Yahweh: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one.

en.L: And these [are] the tumors of gold that [the] Philistines returned [as] a guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one.
en.B: These are the gold tumors that the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath and one for Ekron.
en.R: The Philistines sent back gold tumors as a guilt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. There was one for each of their cities: Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron.

decisions.choice: Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, Ekron: the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: These were the chief cities of the Philistines on the coastal plain, each with its own ruler (verse 4; Joshua 13:3). Ashdod, Gath and Ekron had held the ark (5:1-10).

decisions.choice: tumors: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: Here the written text and the reading tradition agree on the word for tumors used in verse 4.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Readable turns the list into a plain sentence naming the cities.

source.text: וְעַכְבְּרֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֗ב מִסְפַּ֞ר כָּל־עָרֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ לַחֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הַסְּרָנִ֔ים מֵעִ֣יר מִבְצָ֔ר וְעַ֖ד כֹּ֣פֶר הַפְּרָזִ֑י וְעַ֣ד׀אָבֵ֣ל הַגְּדוֹלָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִנִּ֤יחוּ עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ אֵ֚ת אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה בִּשְׂדֵ֥ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בֵּֽית־הַשִּׁמְשִֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] mice of gold, [the] number of all [the] cities of [the] Philistines belonging to the five rulers, from city of fortification and to village of the open country; and as far as Abel the great, which they set down on it [the] ark of Yahweh, until this day, in [the] field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite.

en.L: And the rats of gold [were by the] number of all the cities of [the] Philistines belonging to the five rulers, from fortified city to village of the open country, as far as the great stone on which they set down the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. [It is there] to this day in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite.
en.B: The gold rats matched the number of all the Philistine cities belonging to the five rulers, from fortified cities to country villages, as far as the large stone on which they set the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That stone is still there to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh.
en.R: The gold rats stood for all the Philistine towns that belonged to the five rulers, from walled cities to country villages, all the way to the large rock where the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was set down. That rock is still in Joshua's field at Beth-shemesh to this day.

decisions.choice: the great stone: the stone of verses 14 and 15
alternatives: as far as the great meadow
decisions.reason: The standard Hebrew text has "Abel", a word that means "meadow" or "mourning" and is part of several place names. The two words look very much alike in Hebrew, and some Hebrew manuscripts, the ancient Greek translation and the Aramaic paraphrase read "stone", which fits the large stone already named in verses 14 and 15. The stone is followed here; if "Abel" is kept, it would be a place called "the great meadow" or a name recalling the mourning of verse 19.

decisions.choice: the gold rats ... as far as the great stone: the offering stood for the whole Philistine land, up to the border stone
alternatives: and the great stone is a witness to this day
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence is loosely joined. The rats stood for every Philistine town from walled city to village, and the list reaches as far as the stone on Israel's border where the ark was set down. Another way to take it is that "as far as" introduces a new statement: the great stone is a witness to this day. The ancient Greek reads it that way.

decisions.choice: the number of all the cities: more than five rats, it seems
decisions.reason: Verse 4 spoke of five gold rats, one for each ruler, while this verse links the rats to every town, large and small. The text does not explain the difference; perhaps the rats were added for the smaller towns beyond the five that the tumors stood for.

decisions.choice: to this day: until the time the account was written
decisions.reason: The writer points to something his first readers could still see in their own day: the stone in Joshua's field.

decisions.choice: fortified cities to country villages (Balanced); walled cities to country villages (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Village of the open country" means a village without walls (Deuteronomy 3:5), so the phrase covers every kind of town.

source.text: וַיַּ֞ךְ בְּאַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית־שֶׁ֗מֶשׁ כִּ֤י רָאוּ֙ בַּאֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֤ךְ בָּעָם֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף אִ֑ישׁ וַיִּֽתְאַבְּל֣וּ הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי־הִכָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בָּעָ֖ם מַכָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה

records.literal_gloss: And he struck among [the] men of Beth-shemesh, because they looked into [the] ark of Yahweh, and he struck among the people seventy men, fifty thousand men; and mourned the people, because struck Yahweh among the people a great blow.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck among the men of Beth-shemesh, because they looked into the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck among the people seventy men, 50,000 men. And the people mourned, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck among the people [with] a great blow.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck down some of the men of Beth-shemesh for looking into the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He struck down seventy men among the people, 50,000 men. The people mourned because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck them with such a heavy blow.
en.R: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck down some of the men of Beth-shemesh, because they had looked inside {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ark. He killed seventy men among the people, 50,000 men. The people mourned because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had struck them so hard.

decisions.choice: he struck the men of Beth-shemesh because they looked into the ark
alternatives: the sons of Jeconiah did not rejoice ... and he struck among them
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation begins differently: "And the sons of Jeconiah did not rejoice with the men of Beth-shemesh when they saw the ark of the Lord, and he struck them." On that reading one family is punished for not joining in. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: looked into: gazed at or into what was holy
decisions.reason: The words can mean "looked at" or "looked into"; either way they treated the holy ark as something to stare at. Even the Levites of Kohath were not to look at the holy things or they would die (Numbers 4:20).

decisions.choice: seventy men, fifty thousand men: the Hebrew as it stands, with its difficulty kept
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets "seventy men" and "fifty thousand men" side by side with no "and", which is not how Hebrew normally adds numbers, and Beth-shemesh was a small town. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the Jewish historian Josephus have only seventy, and many think "fifty thousand men" was added to the text later. Others read the two as one total (50,070), or as seventy men out of fifty thousand, or take the word for "thousand" as a clan or military unit (see the note at Numbers 1:46), which would give a much smaller number. The text is kept as it is so the reader can see the problem.

decisions.choice: Yahweh struck: the holiness of the ark cut both ways
decisions.reason: The ark that had brought plague on the Philistines brought death to Israelites who did not treat it as holy. The same lesson returns when Uzzah touches the ark (2 Samuel 6:6-7).

decisions.choice: struck down some of; the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Struck among" means some of them, not all, which Balanced and Readable say. Readable names the LORD as the one who struck, since the Hebrew names him only at the end of the verse.

source.text: וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י בֵֽית־שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ מִ֚י יוּכַ֣ל לַעֲמֹ֔ד לִפְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֧ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים הַקָּד֖וֹשׁ הַזֶּ֑ה וְאֶל־מִ֖י יַעֲלֶ֥ה מֵעָלֵֽינוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] men of Beth-shemesh, Who is able to stand before Yahweh, the God, the holy, this? And to whom will he go up from us?

en.L: And the men of Beth-shemesh said, "Who is able to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, this holy God? And to whom will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} go up from us?"
en.B: Then the men of Beth-shemesh asked, "Who is able to stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, this holy God? And to whom should {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} go up from here, away from us?"
en.R: The men of Beth-shemesh said, "No one can stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, this holy God! Where can we send {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will go away from us?"

decisions.choice: who can stand before Yahweh, this holy God: no one can bear his presence
decisions.reason: To stand before Yahweh is to be in his presence or to serve him there, as the Levites did (Deuteronomy 10:8). The men see that his holiness is dangerous to anyone who treats it lightly.

decisions.choice: he will go up: Yahweh, present with his ark
decisions.reason: The verb can also be read "it will go up", meaning the ark. The two are closely joined in the story, since the ark stood for Yahweh's presence (4:7). Either way, they want it taken away from them, up to another town.

decisions.choice: a statement and a plain question
decisions.reason: Readable turns the first question into the statement it implies and makes the second a practical question about where to send him.

source.text: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־יוֹשְׁבֵ֥י קִרְיַת־יְעָרִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵשִׁ֤בוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה רְד֕וּ הַעֲל֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sent messengers to [the] inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, [The] Philistines have brought back [the] ark of Yahweh; come down, bring it up to you.

en.L: And they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, "[The] Philistines have brought back the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Come down; bring it up to you."
en.B: So they sent messengers to the people of Kiriath-jearim to say, "The Philistines have brought back the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Come down and carry it up to your town."
en.R: Then they sent messengers to the people who lived in Kiriath-jearim. The messengers said, "The Philistines have sent back the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Come down here and take it up to your town."

decisions.choice: Kiriath-jearim: a town in the hills to the northeast of Beth-shemesh
decisions.reason: Kiriath-jearim stood higher up, in the hills toward Jerusalem (Joshua 9:17; 15:9), so the people come "down" and take the ark "up". The ark stayed there until David brought it to Jerusalem (7:1-2; 2 Samuel 6:2).

decisions.choice: the message: good news of the ark's return, with nothing said of the deaths
decisions.reason: The men of Beth-shemesh tell only that the ark is back and ask the other town to take it.

decisions.choice: to your town
decisions.reason: "Up to you" means up to where they live.
